newsitem.title: INDIA: India says U.S. attacks on Iraq regrettable.
newsitem.headline: India says U.S. attacks on Iraq regrettable.

text.p: Indian Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said on Friday that this week's U.S. missile attacks on Iraq were highly regrettable and urged Washington to refrain from further attacks.
"It is highly regrettable. We call upon the United States to refrain from any other attacks on Iraq and to respect its sovereignty and integrity," Gujral told parliament.
"The government of India is unable to accept the justification for the U.S. bombing," Gujral told parliament.

U.S. forces fired a total of 44 cruise missiles at air defence targets in southern Iraq on Tuesday and Wednesday. The attacks were prompted by the Iraqi army's incursion into Kurdish areas in northern Iraq last Saturday.
The Indian foreign ministry had earlier expressed concern at U.S. attacks on Iraq, saying it was likely to affect Middle East peace and security.
Gujral said India was also worried by the attacks because they affected its economic interests and those of Indian workers employed in Gulf region.
"These developments have also had an impact on India. The oil price has gone up," he said.
India imports about 40 percent of its oil and product needs.
Gujral also expressed concern for the Iraqi people, whom he said were suffering under U.N.-imposed sanctions.

"The Iraqi population, including innocent women and children, have been subjected to great hardship and deprivation for many years by U.N. sanctions, and we believe that steps to provide them with relief are long overdue," Gujral said.
Sanctions were imposed on Baghdad when Iraqi troops invaded Kuwait in 1990.
